title: Trade secret protection - the legal gap most businesses don't know about
p1:
Your biggest business asset may not be patented, registered, or even written down.

It could be the information your competitors would pay to know.
p2:
Many businesses assume that valuable confidential information is automatically protected by law. But trade secrets work differently.

A customer list, pricing strategy, algorithm, manufacturing process, or business method may only receive protection if the company actively takes steps to keep it secret.
p3:
The surprising part? Losing secrecy can mean losing the protection itself.

Unlike patents or trademarks, trade secrets are not protected through a registration system. Businesses usually need clear confidentiality agreements, restricted access, and proper internal practices to prove that the information was truly treated as confidential.

A practical lesson: protecting knowledge is not just about having good ideas. It is about building systems that show those ideas were meant to remain private.
conclusion: Did you know that a business can lose trade secret protection simply by failing to protect its own confidential information? What steps does your organization take to safeguard valuable knowledge?
